Include exactly 13 numbers in the response. In the context of a hypothetical, write the jacket blurb for a thriller where a modern day operative of the FBI, ends up back in the early 1960's having to use her knowledge of "future" forensics to leave clues to enable her modern colleagues to catch a time-hopping serial-killer, before he dies.assistant
response:
"When FBI operative Rachel Jenkins is sent back in time to the early 1960s, she finds herself in the midst of a decades-old mystery. A serial killer, known only as 'The Timekeeper,' has been terrorizing the nation, leaving a trail of bodies in his wake. But this is no ordinary killer - he's a time-hopper, able to move through the ages with impunity.

As Rachel navigates the unfamiliar landscape of 1960s America, she must use her knowledge of future forensics to leave clues that will aid her modern colleagues in catching The Timekeeper. But with each passing day, she realizes that she's running out of time - literally. The Timekeeper is always one step ahead, and Rachel's only hope is to outsmart him before he strikes again.

With the help of a local detective, Jack Harris, Rachel must use her skills to unravel the mystery of The Timekeeper's true identity and motivations. But as they dig deeper, they uncover a web of deceit and corruption that goes all the way to the top.

As the body count rises, Rachel and Jack must work together to leave a trail of breadcrumbs for their modern-day colleagues to follow. But with The Timekeeper always lurking in the shadows, can they solve the case before it's too late? The clock is ticking, and the fate of the world hangs in the balance.

Will Rachel and Jack be able to catch The Timekeeper before he strikes again? Or will he continue to leave a trail of death and destruction throughout history? Find out in this heart-pumping, action-packed thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

13 clues, 7 suspects, 5 continents, 3 time zones, 2 detectives, 1 killer, 1 timeline, 1 chance to save the world."
